clue.text: Car is to pull in and be damaged in spin

indicators.note: things damaged are knocked out of shape, so the six words before it are rearranged

explanation.surface: A motoring mishap: a car pulls in and gets damaged while spinning off the road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spin' looks like part of the car's skid, but it is the definition, in the sense of media spin. 'damaged' rearranges CAR IS TO PULL IN BE; 'and' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Spin is slang for the slanted presentation of news that press officers and image consultants practise.

clue.text: Great rap moves involving boy, soon an outcast

indicators.note: involving means the shuffled letters wrap round the following pieces
moves tells us the letters of the words before it shift about into a new order

parts.note: a boy is a son
anon is an old word for soon

explanation.surface: A rapper whose great moves have taken a boy in is soon cast out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moves' is the anagram signal, not dance steps, and 'involving' wraps the shuffled letters round the boy and the old word for soon.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase names a person unwelcome or officially rejected, such as an expelled diplomat, so it fits an outcast.

clue.text: On which people pot trees, we hear

indicators.note: we hear signals that the word is only to be heard, matching another spelling in sound

parts.note: bays are laurel trees

explanation.surface: Gardeners putting trees into pots, as if the clue were about planting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pot' is the snooker sense, sinking a ball, not putting a plant in a container.
explanation.definitionFit: Snooker and pool tables are covered in green woollen cloth, and players pot balls on that surface.

clue.text: Linguistically proficient learner's avoided repeat

indicators.note: avoided means the learner's letter is kept out of the longer word

parts.note: literate means able to read and write well
L is the learner, from the L-plate on a learner driver's car

explanation.surface: A language learner manages to avoid having to repeat a course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'learner's' is 'learner has': the learner, L, has 'avoided' LITERATE, leaving it out.
explanation.definitionFit: To iterate is to do or say again, a formal synonym of the verb repeat.

clue.text: Return once more in dance, pirouetting etc

parts.note: a reel is a lively Scottish dance

indicators.note: a pirouette is a spin on the spot, so the three letters of the following word whirl into a new order

explanation.surface: A dancer returning to the floor, pirouetting and so on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pirouetting' spins the abbreviation into ECT; 'in' is a link joining definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Voters re-elect an official when they return that person to office for another term.

clue.text: I'm much tickled by swimmer having relaxed posture

parts.note: LOL, laughing out loud, is the texting way to say something amuses you
a ling is a fish of the cod family

explanation.surface: Someone tickled pink by a swimmer while lounging about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swimmer' is a fish, not a person in the water; 'by' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Lolling means lounging or sprawling lazily, describing a loose, slack way of sitting or lying.

clue.text: Walk all over right back of large dimensions

indicators.note: back means the abbreviation is read in reverse

parts.note: ample means generously large

explanation.surface: Someone striding all over the right-hand side of a big area.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' reads the abbreviation for right in reverse, though on the surface it seems to mean the rear of a large space.
explanation.definitionFit: To trample is to tread heavily on something, and to walk all over is the same idea, literal or figurative.

clue.text: Icon in the building in a precarious position

indicators.note: building means assembling, so the first three words are put together in a fresh order

explanation.surface: A religious icon kept inside a building that is in a precarious state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'building' looks like the place holding the icon, but it rearranges ICON IN THE.
explanation.definitionFit: Skating on thin ice is the idiom behind it: being somewhere risky that might give way at any moment.

clue.text: Standard French author's nonsense devoured by the famous

indicators.note: devoured by means eaten up, so the author and nonsense end up inside the famous

parts.note: stars are famous people
George Sand was a French novelist; with the possessive she gives SANDS
tripe is rubbish or nonsense

explanation.surface: A French writer's drivel swallowed whole by celebrities.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Standard' is a flag, not a norm. SANDS TRIPE goes between STAR and the final S.
explanation.definitionFit: A standard is a flag or banner, and this is the popular name of the flag of the United States.

clue.text: With an increase in wages, this man's going to cause chaos

parts.note: a raise is an increase in pay
he'll is a contraction of he will, this man is going to

explanation.surface: A worker given a pay rise who is still going to kick up a fuss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With' is a link; the contraction HE'LL loses its apostrophe in the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: To raise hell is an idiom for creating an uproar or causing havoc.

clue.text: Hollow areas in the Appalachian Trail

indicators.note: in shows the letters sit inside the following words, across the gap between them

explanation.surface: Caves and hollows found along the Appalachian Trail hiking route.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the' is a link; the letters straddle Appalachi-AN TRA-il.
explanation.definitionFit: Antra is the plural of antrum, an anatomical cavity or sinus, such as a hollow in bone.

clue.text: Naked paramour and judge did stuff

indicators.note: naked means stripped of covering, so the word for paramour loses its outer letters

parts.note: a paramour is a lover
to rate is to judge or assess

explanation.surface: A scandal: a naked lover and a judge up to something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Naked' strips the lover of its outer letters; 'and' is a link. 'did stuff' means stuffed oneself with food.
explanation.definitionFit: To stuff yourself is to eat too much, so 'did stuff' is a past-tense way of saying ate to excess.

clue.text: You can't trust a naughty child's hints

parts.note: an imp is a mischievous child; the possessive makes what follows the imp's
lies are what can't be trusted

explanation.surface: Warning that clues dropped by a mischievous child are not to be relied on.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as one sentence, but splits into the imp's lies, which you can't trust.
explanation.definitionFit: To hint at something is to suggest it without stating it, which is what the verb implies does.

clue.text: Like some wine drunk by crook helping holy work

indicators.note: something drunk by another goes inside it, so the wine word sits within the crook and helping

parts.note: a con is a convict or swindler, a crook
a ration is an allotted portion, a helping
sec describes dry wine

explanation.surface: A crook drinking communion wine while helping with church duties.
explanation.walkthrough: Dry wine is described as sec, a French term used on wine labels; 'drunk by' sets it inside the other two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Consecration is the sacred act of dedicating something to God, such as blessing bread and wine or a church.

clue.text: Married wearing collar one's found on a sofa

indicators.note: the outer word is worn over the letter for married, so it goes round it

parts.note: to collar a suspect is to arrest him

explanation.surface: A married man wearing a collar is discovered on the couch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'collar' is the police verb, not a garment.
explanation.definitionFit: A sofa has a padded support at each end for resting the elbow on.

clue.text: One of the top three celebs touring lake next to the sea

indicators.note: next to puts the sea right beside the celebrity piece

parts.note: the Med is the Mediterranean Sea

indicators.note: touring means going round, so the celebrities enclose the lake

parts.note: the A-list is the top tier of celebrities

explanation.surface: A podium finisher's celebrity friends touring a lake beside the sea.
explanation.walkthrough: The A-list is the top tier of celebrities; 'touring' wraps it round the lake and 'next to' sets the sea in front.
explanation.definitionFit: First, second and third places at the Olympics earn gold, silver and bronze awards.

clue.text: See 13
Attic in which old lady hides gems from the east

indicators.note: hides means the grandmother conceals the gems inside her

parts.note: gran is a grandmother

indicators.note: read from the east, an across word runs right to left, so it is reversed

parts.note: ice is slang for diamonds

explanation.surface: A loft where an old lady has hidden jewels brought from the Orient.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Attic' looks like the loft, but means of Attica, around Athens. 'from the east' reverses the gems, giving ECI.
explanation.definitionFit: Attic describes Attica and Athens, so it is a near synonym for Greek, especially of ancient style.

clue.text: See 13
Diabolical figure in prison no longer?

parts.note: old means former, no longer current
the nick is British slang for prison or a police station

explanation.surface: Asks whether the devilish inmate has left jail.
explanation.walkthrough: A former prison would be an old nick; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Old Nick is a traditional nickname for the Devil, Satan.

clue.text: Uttered like a monk with a soft spot for Kelly

parts.note: into means keen on or fond of
Ned Kelly was the Australian outlaw

explanation.surface: A monk fond of someone called Kelly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kelly' needs a forename: Ned Kelly, the famous Australian bushranger.
explanation.definitionFit: Monks chant prayers on a single note, and intoned means spoken or sung in that monotone way.

clue.text: Ties last of livestock on board

indicators.note: last of picks the final letter of the word that follows

parts.note: on board means in a ship

explanation.surface: Tying down the last of the animals on board a vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ties' is a noun, family bonds, not a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Family ties are the bonds of blood relationship between relatives.

clue.text: Set out to host dear foreign people who make an impression

indicators.note: to host is to have a guest inside, so the rearranged letters enclose the next piece
out here means out of order, so the three letters are rearranged

parts.note: cher is French for dear

explanation.surface: Someone setting out to entertain a beloved foreigner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges the first word into ETS, and 'to host' wraps that round the French word for dear.
explanation.definitionFit: Etching artists cut designs into metal plates and print them, so they literally make impressions.

clue.text: Impose fee on Roman Catholic, when straying

indicators.note: straying means wandering off course, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Charging a fee to a wandering Catholic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'straying' rearranges FEE ON RC; 'when' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To enforce a rule or penalty is to impose it and make people comply.

clue.text: Sing with Italian sopranos covering heavy metal

indicators.note: covering means the Italian word and the sopranos together go round the metal

parts.note: con is Italian for with
S is the abbreviation for soprano, so two give SS
Fe is the chemical symbol for iron, a heavy metal

explanation.surface: An Italian choir with sopranos singing over the din of heavy metal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sing' is underworld slang for telling the police, not music. 'covering' wraps the Italian word and sopranos round the iron symbol.
explanation.definitionFit: In criminal slang, to sing is to inform or admit everything, as a suspect does under questioning.

clue.text: See 13
Edible substance to take shape, a preserve

parts.note: to gel is to set or take definite form
to tin food is to preserve it in a can

explanation.surface: A jelly-like food that sets into shape and keeps well.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' is a link; 'preserve' is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Gelatin is the protein from animal collagen used to set jellies and desserts, so it is eaten.

clue.text: Ultimately golf, not cricket, is a source of entertainment

indicators.note: ultimately means in the end, so take the final letter

parts.note: not cricket is a British idiom for unfair or unsporting

explanation.surface: A sporting fan concluding that golf, rather than cricket, is the real entertainment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not cricket' is a British idiom meaning unfair, nothing to do with sport; 'is' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A travelling fairground with rides, stalls and sideshows exists to amuse visitors.

clue.text: Pale like one prone to brooding

parts.note: as means like, in the same way as
a hen broods, sitting on eggs to hatch them

explanation.surface: A moody person compared to someone pale and inclined to sulk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brooding' is the bird sitting on eggs, not moody thought.
explanation.definitionFit: Ashen describes a face drained of colour, grey as ash, so it means pale.

clue.text: Film has an entertaining story

indicators.note: entertaining means having a guest inside, so the article holds the story

parts.note: a story can be a fib, a lie

explanation.surface: A movie with an amusing plot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'entertaining' looks like 'amusing' but means holding inside; 'story' is a fib. 'has' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Ridley Scott's 1979 science-fiction horror movie about a creature aboard a spaceship has this title.

clue.text: Flog drug, weak joint

parts.note: horse is slang for heroin
the hip is a joint

explanation.surface: A dealer selling a feeble cannabis joint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flog' looks like 'sell' beside 'drug' and 'joint', but means whip; 'joint' is a body part.
explanation.definitionFit: To horsewhip someone is to beat them with a whip, which is what flog means here.

clue.text: They pick up article by current media workers

parts.note: an is the indefinite article
a tide is a current of water
the press is the news media
worker ants, hence ants as workers

explanation.surface: Journalists collecting an article from a current affairs story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pick up' means cheer up, not collect; 'by' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Mood-lifting drugs relieve depression, so they give the patient a pick-me-up.
